title: The 'I Don't Know' Suppression Effect: Does Adding a Persona Reduce Honest Abstention?

original_idea.body: The 'I Don't Know' Suppression Effect. Problem: whether assigning a confident expert persona specifically reduces honest abstention on hard questions is open. Direction: on hard factual items where abstention is honest, compare neutral assistant vs confident-expert persona, measure abstention and confident-wrong rate, isolating the persona's effect on honest uncertainty disclosure.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: persona-driven abstention suppression is a concrete harmful failure (expert chatbot that never says IDK).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Neutral vs persona prompt comparison on hard QA; prompting only.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model prompt-only audit connecting two literatures.

novelty.reasoning: Both component findings exist; the persona-x-abstention interaction may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The two component effects are published; their interaction (persona reducing abstention) is plausibly open.
